extracted.subtask_description: Datelined Associated Press wartime dispatches reporting military invasions, occupations, official communiques, eyewitness accounts, civilian responses, and policy consequences across multiple Scandinavian and European locations during WWII-era events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat unconfirmed reports with reserve
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that Norway was preparing to negotiate with Germany "should be treated with great reserve." There was no confirmation in the British capital of such a Norwegian move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag unverified claims explicitly, avoid treating rumors as fact, and seek confirmation from authoritative sources before asserting. Example anti-pattern: publishing speculation about negotiations as fact without corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and wire-service attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear datelines and attributions such as "BERLIN April 10 (A. P.).—" or "COPENHAGEN, April 10—" to indicate origin and service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include location and date at the start of dispatches and attribute to the reporting agency/correspondent. This orients readers and shows source provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute to authoritative official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite "British official quarters", "authorized sources", "Norwegian military quarters" when reporting denials, confirmations, or official positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, name the office or describe its authority. Report both confirmations and denials from official channels to show the balance of available evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and label eyewitness accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Include eyewitness reporting such as "Eyewitness accounts of the attack..." and "Swedish fishermen... counted ten big gray German transports", while making clear their origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present first-hand accounts with attribution and context; indicate when eyewitness reports conflict or are provisional. Do not conflate eyewitness anecdotes with verified facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report official communiques and casualty claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Report communiques like "Norwegian military quarters issued a communique saying 200 Germans were killed" and similar official casualty or engagement statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish official communique text or summaries, but mark casualty and loss figures as reported and subject to verification. Provide source and whether figures are confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide historical and contextual background
rubrics_metrics.description: Give background such as North Schleswig's 1920 plebiscite results: "North Schleswig voted 75,431 to 25,329 in 1920 to go to Denmark..." to explain territorial claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise historical context that helps readers understand current claims, disputes, or territorial issues. Use archival numbers and sources where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe civilian impact and public reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Depict civilian conditions: "Panic-stricken residents of Oslo... Long columns of cars, trucks and busses began taking the civilians still in Oslo from the city."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on evacuations, panic, sheltering, refugee flows, and public mood to convey human consequences of events. Use eyewitness and official sources; avoid sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include military details with caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Report military hardware and engagements: references to "one vessel of the Deutschland class", "sinking two of the transports and a destroyer", while noting when reports are unconfirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide types of ships, approximate losses, and engagement outcomes but qualify with source reliability. If specifics are unknown, say so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesize multiple correspondents and geographic perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile dispatches from varied locations (Berlin, London, Copenhagen, Stockholm, Washington, New York, Paris) to present a fuller picture of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reporting from multiple datelines to cross-check facts and provide regional nuance. Make the provenance of each piece clear to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include precise timings and sequence of events
rubrics_metrics.description: Report specific times and sequencing such as "The city was ordered emptied of its population at 11.15 A.M. (5.15 A.M E.S.T.)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When available, include exact times (with time zones) to help readers understand chronology. Note when times are estimates or reported by sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report government emergency measures and directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail measures like "decrees forbidding price raising and restricting gasoline sales" and blackout orders or restrictions on travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish what governments decree during crises (curfews, rationing, price controls), including scope and duration, so readers know practical impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote leaders and officials directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Use direct quotations from leaders: e.g., Premier statements and remarks such as "We can hope that the dis... will be preserved for our children." and Reynaud's remarks to the Senate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include verbatim quotes for authority and clarity; attribute them precisely (who, where, when). Contextualize quotes to avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report diplomatic/policy responses and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe policy moves such as the U.S. proclamation extending the European combat zone and administrative attitudes like Jesse Jones's 'stop, look and listen' approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how events trigger diplomatic, legal, or policy responses and the practical consequences (e.g., shipping restrictions). Provide authoritative sources for such decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note information flow constraints and censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention communication disruptions and curtailed news: "Copenhagen’s communications with the outside world were cut" and "newspapers published only reduced editions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform readers about limits on reporting (cut lines, censorship, blackout) that affect the completeness and timeliness of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify geographic extents with coordinates when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Give geographic extents precisely: "extends around the Scandinavian peninsula to the Russian mainland just south of 44 degrees east longitude and 70 degrees north latitude."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting area designations (combat zones, embargo areas), provide coordinates or clear boundaries so readers and stakeholders can understand scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label unverified numeric claims clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: When giving figures (troop losses, ship tonnage, number of transports), the story uses qualifiers like "unconfirmed report indicated", "could not be verified", "reported to have".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always attach qualifiers to provisional numeric claims and indicate the source. Prefer phrasing such as "reported" or "according to [source]" rather than asserting uncertain numbers as facts.
